why.title: Thousands of children have words they cannot say aloud
why.body: Many special children in Bangladesh understand far more than they can express. Without a way to communicate, their needs, feelings, and ideas stay locked inside — at home, in classrooms, everywhere. Communication is not a luxury; it is the foundation of learning, dignity, and inclusion.

solution.title: A voice in their own language
solution.body: Voice Assistant is a free, fully offline AAC app built by MIST researchers. A child taps a picture — the app speaks it aloud in natural Bangla or English. Sixteen communication categories, alphabet learning for both languages, a writing canvas, and words families can customize with their own photos and voices.

showcase.title: Built around how children actually communicate
showcase.note: Every board speaks aloud in Bangla with an English option — and works completely offline.

research.title: Engineering grounded in evidence
research.body: The project is developed at the Department of Biomedical Engineering, MIST, through needs assessment with special-education teachers, families, and therapists — from Bengali speech synthesis tuning to sensory-friendly interface design.

fallback.story:
Voice Assistant grew out of conversations with special-education teachers and parents in Dhaka, who described the same frustration again and again: their children understood so much more than they could say. The Department of Biomedical Engineering at MIST set out to build something different — an app that speaks a child's own language, works without an internet connection, and costs families nothing.

What started as a research prototype is now a growing project: devices prepared, activated, and handed directly to children and their schools, with the team following up to learn what works and what needs to change.
fallback.mission: To give every special child in Bangladesh a reliable, dignified way to communicate — in Bangla, in English, anywhere, without needing a connection to do it.
fallback.acknowledgments: This project would not exist without the special-education teachers, therapists, and families who shared their time and insight, and the Department of Biomedical Engineering, Military Institute of Science and Technology, for its continued support.

hero.title: A voice that fits in a backpack
hero.lede: Voice Assistant is a free, offline AAC (Augmentative and Alternative Communication) app — built so a child can carry their voice anywhere, no internet required.

challenge.title: Understanding is not the same as being understood
challenge.body: Many special children process language just fine — what's missing is a reliable way to produce it. Existing communication tools are often expensive, English-only, or need a constant internet connection few Bangladeshi families can rely on. The result: children who have so much to say, and no way to say it.

solution.title: Tap a picture. Hear a voice.
solution.body: A child taps a picture card — the app speaks the word aloud immediately, in natural-sounding Bangla or English, tuned with a softer, child-like pitch. Everything runs on the device itself: no data plan, no waiting, no dependency on a signal that might not reach a rural classroom.

categories.title: Every board speaks a child's everyday world

study.title: Bangla and English literacy, built in
study.body: Beyond communication boards, the app teaches the Bangla alphabet (স্বরবর্ণ ও ব্যঞ্জনবর্ণ) and English letters with playful reveal animations, plus a free-form writing and drawing canvas.

custom.title: Families add their own words
custom.body: Parents and teachers can add custom words with their own photos and recorded voices — a sibling's name, a favorite snack, a specific bus route. The app becomes a picture of that child's actual life, not a generic template.

offline.title: Works completely offline
offline.body: No wifi at school? No mobile data at home? It doesn't matter. Every word, every voice, every lesson is stored on the device itself from the moment it's activated.

handover.title: How a device reaches a child
handover.body: Each tablet is prepared, loaded, and activated by the team before it ever reaches a family — a unique activation key ties the device to the project, and it works from the very first tap.

hero.title: Privacy & Child Safety Policy
hero.lede: How we collect, use, and protect information on this website — and the extra safeguards we apply to any photo or story involving a child.

whoWeAre.title: Who we are
whoWeAre.body: This website is run by the Voice Assistant project team in the Department of Biomedical Engineering, Military Institute of Science and Technology (MIST), Dhaka, Bangladesh. Voice Assistant is a free, offline, Bangla-first AAC (Augmentative and Alternative Communication) app built to help special-needs children communicate. This page explains how we handle information on this website — it does not describe how the Voice Assistant mobile app itself works, since the app runs entirely offline on a user's own device and never sends any personal data anywhere.

dataWeCollect.title: Information we collect
dataWeCollect.body:
We collect information in three ways.

1. Contact & device-request forms — when you use our contact form, we collect your name, email address, and whatever else you choose to share (organization, phone number, and your message). If you're requesting a device on behalf of a child, we may ask for basic details needed to coordinate the handover.

2. Photos, videos, and stories — we publish photos and videos from handover events, workshops, and stories from the families and professionals we work with. Any photo or video that could identify a child is never published without the written, informed consent of a parent or guardian — see "How we handle photos and videos of children" below.

3. Minimal website cookies — we use only two small, functional cookies: one remembers your light/dark display preference, and one remembers whether you're viewing the site in English or Bangla. We do not use analytics, advertising, or tracking cookies of any kind, and we do not share your browsing activity with any third party.

childConsent.title: How we handle photos and videos of children
childConsent.body:
We take this seriously, and it's built directly into how our website works, not just a promise in this document.

No photo or video featuring an identifiable child is ever published without a signed consent form from a parent or guardian, kept on file by our team.

This is enforced technically, not just by policy — our content system will not let staff publish media marked as featuring a child unless that consent has been explicitly confirmed, and the website independently re-checks this before showing any image publicly.

If you're a parent or guardian and would like a photo or video of your child removed, or want to know what we have on file, contact us (details below) and we'll act on it promptly.

howWeUse.title: How we use your information
howWeUse.body: We use the information you share with us only to respond to your inquiry, coordinate a device handover or support request, and — only with your explicit permission — to feature your story on this website. We do not use your contact information for marketing, and we do not sell, rent, or trade it to anyone.

sharing.title: Who we share information with
sharing.body: We do not sell or share your personal information with third parties for their own purposes. Our website runs on standard cloud infrastructure providers (for hosting, database storage, and — if you request a device — coordinating that request), who process data only on our instructions and only as needed to run the site.

retentionSecurity.title: How we protect and retain information
retentionSecurity.body: We keep contact-form submissions only as long as needed to respond to you and coordinate any follow-up, and we apply reasonable technical and organizational safeguards — secure hosting, access limited to our team, encrypted connections — to protect it. No online system can be guaranteed 100% secure, but we work to keep your information as safe as we reasonably can.

yourRights.title: Your rights
yourRights.body: You can ask us, at any time, what information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it — including withdrawing consent for a photo or story and having it taken down. Just reach out using the contact details below.

childrenDirect.title: Children's use of this website
childrenDirect.body: This website is intended for parents, teachers, clinicians, and organizations — not for direct use by children. We do not knowingly collect personal information directly from children through this website; the photos and videos described above are shared with us by parents, guardians, or professionals working with a child, never collected from a child directly.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: We may update this policy as the project grows. If we make a meaningful change, we'll update the "last updated" date at the top of this page.

contact.title: Contact us
contact.body: Questions about this policy, or requests about your own information, are welcome any time — reach us through our Contact page, or directly through the Department of Biomedical Engineering, MIST.
